Defendant Wu Suet-ting appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black mask. The charges allege that on July 10 and August 17, the defendant failed to keep a yellow male crossbred dog under control with a leash no longer than two metres in length, allowing it to enter an area near YOHO Mall in Yuen Long. She faces two counts of "allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place."

The prosecution applied for an adjournment of ten weeks for the next mention and did not oppose bail. Deputy Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to October 29 for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for "allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place" carries a maximum penalty of a HK$25,000 fine and three months' imprisonment.

Ye Yin, Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, said yesterday that if a dog owner decides to surrender a large dog to the government, the department would consider options including humane euthanasia. If the owner intends to reclaim the dog, the animal could be classified as a "known dangerous dog," and the court may order that it wear a muzzle when outdoors in the future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection group毛守救援 (Mao Shou Rescue), said in an interview with集誌社 that the dog owner has already expressed regret over signing the abandonment form. He also said Mao Shou Rescue is willing to take in the dog and will provide a dog trainer to assist with its rehabilitation.
